figures.title: f splits columns, g splits rows, one all-reduce closes the block
figures.caption: A tensor-parallel linear layer in two steps. f splits W by columns, so rank i computes y_i = xW_i with shape B×(K/N) and no collective. g splits V by rows, so each rank produces a partial sum z_i of shape B×M and an all-reduce sums them. The count is fixed at two collectives per block, 64 per forward for a 32-block model; the volume per collective is 2(N−1)/N × B×H per rank, which is B×H at N = 2 and 1.75 B×H at N = 8.
figures.alt: Three lanes across five steps. Rank 0 and rank 1 both start from the same x of shape B by H. In the f step each multiplies x by its own column slice of W, giving y-zero and y-one of shape B by K over N. In the g step each multiplies its y by its row slice of V, giving partial sums z-zero and z-one of shape B by M. The all-reduce step sums the partials on rank 0 while rank 1 waits; the link lane carries 2 times N minus 1 over N times B by H elements per rank. The next block repeats the pair.

data.note: At N = 2 the ring sends B×H elements per rank per collective; at N = 8 it sends 1.75 B×H. A 70B model at four bits reads 35 GB of weights per token, so on an H100 at 3,350 GB/s the step floor is 10.4 ms. Over 32 blocks and two collectives that is 64 collectives and a budget of 10.4/64 = 0.1625 ms, or 162.5 µs, per collective. Above that round trip the schedule cannot reach the memory-bound floor.

anim.intro: Press Play or Next to follow one tensor-parallel block through its two collectives.

steps.label: x of shape B×H is replicated on both ranks. Nothing has been split yet.
f splits W by columns into N slices W_i of shape H×(K/N). Rank i computes y_i = xW_i of shape B×(K/N), and no rank needs another's slice, so there is no collective here.
g splits V by rows into slices of shape (K/N)×M. Rank i computes z_i = y_i V_i of shape B×M, a partial sum over its slice of the input features.

One all-reduce sums the partials: z = sum of z_i. A ring sends 2(N−1)/N × B×H per rank, which is B×H at N = 2 and 1.75 B×H at N = 8. Two collectives per block over 32 blocks is 64 per forward pass, so the 10.4 ms floor allows 10.4/64 = 0.1625 ms = 162.5 µs per collective.
The block is closed and both ranks hold the full B×M output, so the next block starts from a replicated x again. Two collectives per block, fixed in count but not in volume as N grows.

figures.title: Tensor parallelism pays per collective; pipeline pays per bubble
figures.caption: Tensor parallelism splits each layer's matrices and needs an all-reduce after every g: two collectives per block, 64 per forward for 32 blocks, which leaves 162.5 µs of the 10.4 ms step per collective. Pipeline parallelism splits layers across ranks and needs a point-to-point send per micro-batch boundary; with P stages and M micro-batches the idle fraction is (P−1)/(M+P−1), 3 of 11 slots at P = 4, M = 8 and 3 of 19 at M = 16.
figures.alt: Two panels. The tensor-parallel panel lists: f computes y-i equals x W-i with W-i of shape H by K over N; g computes partial sums; an all-reduce follows each g; two collectives per block and 64 per 32-block forward; the per-collective budget is 162.5 microseconds; the ring moves 2 times N minus 1 over N times B by H. The pipeline panel lists: each rank holds whole layers; one send per micro-batch boundary; M times P minus 1 sends per direction; the bubble is P minus 1 over M plus P minus 1; 3 of 11 slots idle at four stages and eight micro-batches, 3 of 19 at sixteen.

items: f: y_i = xW_i, W_i is H×(K/N)
g: z_i = y_iV_i, partial sums of shape B×M

panels.title: Pipeline parallel: per-bubble idle
panels.note: Doubling M cuts the bubble from 27% to 16%, a factor of about 1.7, not half. With P = 2 and L = 32, tensor parallelism issues 64 collective operations for every pipeline send.

data.note: The per-collective budget moves with the model, the batch and the collective size; it is not a general link threshold. A split that halves compute time but doubles stall time pays only while stall is below half the compute time it removes.

anim.intro: Press Play or Next to price tensor parallelism against pipeline parallelism.

steps.label: Tensor parallel: f is y_i = xW_i with W_i of shape H×(K/N) and no collective; g is z_i = y_iV_i, partial sums of shape B×M, followed by one all-reduce. That is 2 collectives per block.

Over 32 blocks that is 64 collectives. The 70B model at four bits reads 35 GB per token, which at 3,350 GB/s floors the step at 10.4 ms, so each collective has 10.4/64 = 0.1625 ms = 162.5 µs. Above that round trip the schedule cannot reach the floor.

Ring volume grows with N: 2(N−1)/N × B×H is B×H at N = 2 and 1.75 B×H at N = 8. Pipeline parallel instead puts whole layers on each rank and sends once per micro-batch boundary, M(P−1) sends per direction per step.

The pipeline's cost is the bubble. With P stages and M micro-batches the step takes M + P − 1 slots and P − 1 are idle, so idle fraction is (P−1)/(M+P−1): P = 4, M = 8 gives 3/11 = 27.3%, and M = 16 gives 3/19 = 15.8%. Doubling M cuts idle time by well under half.

sources.note: Shoeybi et al., Megatron-LM (2019): the column-parallel f and row-parallel g split with one all-reduce per block.
Narayanan et al., Efficient Large-Scale Language Model Training on GPU Clusters (2021): pipeline bubble arithmetic and the tensor-inside-node, pipeline-across-node hybrid.
